The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W10-3/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W10-3/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
* At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
* At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.
**How the architecture components interact with each other**
The *Sequence Diagram* below shows how the components interact with each other for the scenario where the user issues the command `delete 1`.
Each of the four main components (also shown in the diagram above),
* defines its *API* in an `interface` with the same name as the Component.
* provides its functionality through a concrete `{Component Name}Manager` class that implements the corresponding API interface.

For example, the `Logic` component defines its API in `Logic.java` and implements it in `LogicManager.java`. Other components interact with a component through its interface rather than its concrete class, preventing them from coupling to that component's implementation, as illustrated in the following partial class diagram.
The sections below give more details of each component.
The **API** of this component is specified in [`Ui.java`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W10-3/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/Ui.java)

The UI consists of a `MainWindow` and its parts: `CommandBox`, `ResultDisplay`, `PersonListPanel` with its `PersonCard`s, `PersonDetailsPanel`, and `StatusBarFooter`, plus a separate `HelpWindow`. All of these, including `MainWindow`, inherit from the abstract `UiPart` class, which captures common behavior among classes that represent visible GUI parts.

`MainWindow` also holds the sidebar with the Active Students, Upcoming Lessons, and Archived Students buttons. Each button runs `list`, `upcoming`, or `list archived` through the same method as a typed command, so the feedback and displayed indices are the same, and the highlighted button follows the view shown by the last command. `PersonDetailsPanel` shows the read-only details of the student selected in `PersonListPanel`, which keeps that student selected when the displayed list changes. `PersonCard` and `PersonDetailsPanel` format a student through the shared `StudentDisplayFormatter`, so missing values and overdue lessons look the same in both.

The window can shrink to `820 × 450` so that it fits a `1280 × 720` screen at 150% scaling, and `MainWindow` limits the saved or default window size to the primary screen when it opens. To stay readable at that size, `ResultDisplay` shows two lines before it scrolls, `PersonCard` wraps tags in a row below the name so that tags cannot hide the name, and very long tags are shortened with `...` in both the card and `PersonDetailsPanel`. Font sizes stay fixed, so a card shortens long text with `...` when it runs out of width.

The `UI` component uses the JavaFX UI framework. The layouts of these UI parts are defined in matching `.fxml` files in `src/main/resources/view`. For example, [`MainWindow.fxml`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W10-3/tp/tree/master/src/main/resources/view/MainWindow.fxml) specifies the layout of [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W10-3/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/MainWindow.java).

Commands that leave the address book unchanged, such as `list` or `exit`, do not write the data file, so a data file that could not be loaded stays on disk until the user changes data. If saving fails, it restores the in-memory snapshot before reporting the save failure, so the UI returns to the state before the command. The data file may already have been partially written, so the previously saved data is not guaranteed to be preserved.
1. The result of the command execution is encapsulated as a `CommandResult` object which is returned from `Logic`.

### Add command validation and offline help
`CommandArgumentTokenizer` scans for one- or two-character lower-case prefix tokens at the start of an argument or
after whitespace. It is shared by `add`, `edit`, and `filter`, rejects unsupported tokens, and stores the preamble and
field values in an `ArgumentMultimap`. Text inside a pair of double quotes is treated as one field value, so a subject
or address can contain text such as `l/` or `n/` without being split into another field. The enclosing quotes are not
stored. Longer slash-terminated words such as `Level/` are ordinary text rather than CLI prefixes. Inside an `n/` or `gn/`
value, the whole-word relationship markers `s/o`, `d/o`, `a/l`, and `a/p` are also ordinary text, so names such as
`Raj s/o Kumar` are not split at the `s/` subject prefix or rejected as an unsupported `d/` prefix. Outside a name, the
same tokens are still read as prefixes.

Validation follows a fixed order: token structure, required `n/`, repeated prefixes, guardian-name dependency, then individual field values. Duplicate-prefix errors list the repeated tokens in a stable order. Names and addresses have surrounding whitespace removed and internal whitespace collapsed before validation. Subjects have surrounding whitespace removed and repeated ordinary spaces collapsed, so a tab or other control character inside a subject still reaches `Subject` validation and is rejected. `Person#isSamePerson` compares names after the same whitespace normalization and case folding; phone, email, and guardian details do not determine whether two students are duplicates. An invalid command fails before `AddCommand` can update the model or save data.

`HelpWindow` bundles the command formats and important rules in its FXML layout, so help is available without a network connection. `HelpCommand` only asks the UI to open the window and confirms this in the result panel. `LogicManager` returns the help result without saving the address book, which also allows help when the existing data file cannot be loaded.

TutorContacts represents a student's guardian as an immutable `Guardian` value object containing a required `Name` and optional `Phone` and `Email` values. `Person` stores the whole value as `Optional<Guardian>`, so the model cannot represent guardian contact details without a guardian name.

The `add` command accepts the feature-specific prefixes `gn/`, `gp/`, and `ge/`. `AddCommandParser` first rejects duplicate single-valued prefixes, then enforces the dependency that `gp/` and `ge/` require `gn/`. `ParserUtil` applies the existing name, phone, and email validation rules before constructing the `Guardian`.

`JsonAdaptedPerson` stores guardian name, phone, and email as separate nullable JSON properties. All three properties may be absent when loading older files. If a saved file contains a guardian phone or email without a guardian name, loading fails rather than creating an invalid domain object.

`PersonCard` displays all three guardian fields. Missing guardian values are shown as `Not provided` only in the UI; that display text is never written to the data file. Existing commands that replace a `Person`, such as `edit`, must carry the unchanged guardian value forward.

TutorContacts represents tutoring context using immutable `Subject` and `EducationLevel` value objects. `Person` stores each value independently as an `Optional`, allowing a tutor to record either field, both fields, or neither field.

The `add` command accepts `s/` for a subject and `l/` for an education level. `ParserUtil` trims both values before validation. Subjects must be non-blank, contain no control characters, and contain at most 100 characters. Education levels accept `P1`–`P6`, `S1`–`S5`, or `JC1`–`JC2` case-insensitively and are normalized to uppercase.

`JsonAdaptedPerson` stores the two values as separate nullable JSON properties, so valid data files created before these fields were introduced remain loadable. `PersonCard` displays `Not provided` for an absent value without writing that placeholder to storage. Commands that replace a `Person`, such as `edit`, preserve both values unchanged.

value objects. `Person` stores both values as independent `Optional` fields, so either field may be recorded or omitted.
Each present value contains 1–200 characters and rejects ISO control characters while allowing ordinary spaces and

* Pros: Matches the target user's need to see the next arrangement for each student, keeps commands short, and

* Cons: Lesson history and recurring lessons cannot be represented.

`ModelManager` maintains a `FilteredList<Person>` wrapped by a `SortedList<Person>` and exposes the sorted list as the
current result view. It records whether the view's `ResultViewScope` is `ACTIVE` or `ARCHIVED`. `list`, `find`, `filter`,
and `upcoming` use the active scope; `list archived` uses the archived scope. The scope predicate is combined with the
command's query predicate, so archived students cannot appear in active queries. Updating a filter first clears any
existing comparator, which returns `list`, `find`, `filter`, and `list archived` to saved order. `upcoming` then applies
its lesson-time comparator. `PersonListPanel` derives each visible one-based index from the displayed list position.
Partial-name matching converts both names and keywords using `Locale.ROOT` and applies substring matching. Multiple
keywords use OR. Because each `Person` is evaluated once by one predicate, repeated or overlapping keywords cannot
duplicate a result. `FindCommandParser` still matches a keyword that starts with a command prefix, such as `n/alex`,
because names may contain markers such as `s/o`; it only marks the command so that an empty result suggests plain
keywords and `filter`. Subject and education-level filters use exact normalized matching and combine two supplied fields
with AND; an absent field cannot satisfy a supplied criterion.
Index-based commands obtain their target from `Model#getFilteredPersonList`, so edit, delete, archive, schedule, and
unschedule after a query act on the record carrying the displayed index, including when `upcoming` has reordered the
students. A new query replaces the previous predicate and order; `list` restores the complete active view in saved
Active-only mutations check the scope before resolving an index: `edit`, `archive`, `schedule`, and `unschedule` reject
the archived view, while `unarchive` requires it. Permanent `delete` remains available in either scope. Cross-feature
tests verify targets selected from find, filter, upcoming, and archived views, including archive removal, lesson
changes, sorted indices, and the reset from one query to another.

* Cons: A lesson whose time passes while the list is showing stays in the list, marked overdue, until `upcoming`
* **Alternative 2:** Re-filter the upcoming list after every command.
* Pros: The list never contains a lesson that has already started.

the tutor that the lesson was missed, so they can reschedule or clear it.

* Pros: Lessons leave the list as soon as they start.
* Cons: The indices can change while the user is typing, so a command such as `delete 2` could act on a different

TutorContacts is an **offline desktop application for private tutors to manage student and guardian contact details, optimized for use through a Command Line Interface (CLI)** while retaining the benefits of a Graphical User Interface (GUI).
New to TutorContacts? Start with [Quick start](#quick-start) and [The main window](#the-main-window), then use the
table below to jump to the task you need.
| Record a new student | `add` | [Adding a student](#adding-a-student-add) |
| Update or clear a student's details | `edit` | [Editing a student](#editing-a-student-edit) |
| Find students by name, subject, or level | `find`, `filter` | [Locating students](#locating-students-by-name-find), [Filtering students](#filtering-students-by-tutoring-details-filter) |
| Plan the next lesson | `schedule`, `unschedule`, `upcoming` | [Scheduling a lesson](#scheduling-a-lesson-schedule) |
| Keep a former student without deleting them | `archive`, `list archived`, `unarchive` | [Archiving a student](#archiving-a-student-archive) |
| Remove records permanently | `delete`, `clear` | [Deleting a student](#deleting-a-student-delete), [Clearing all entries](#clearing-all-entries-clear) |

* Words in `UPPER_CASE` are the parameters to be supplied by the user.
For example, in `add n/NAME`, replace `NAME` with a value such as `John Doe`.
* Items in square brackets are optional.
For example, `n/NAME [t/TAG]…​` can be used as `n/John Doe t/friend t/online` or as `n/John Doe`.
* The prefixes in `add` can be in any order, with whitespace between fields.
For example, `add p/81234567 n/Alex Tan` is accepted. Every `add` prefix except `t/` can appear only once.
* Prefixes contain one or two lower-case characters followed by `/`. If a field value contains separate text that
looks like a prefix, wrap the complete value in double quotes.
For example, use `a/"Block n/7"`. The quotes are not stored. Longer words such as `Level/` do not need quotes.
* Commands that take no parameters, namely `help`, `exit`, `clear`, and `upcoming`, reject any extra text.
For example, `help 123`, `clear 3`, and `upcoming 3` are rejected without changing any data.
`list` accepts only no argument or the exact argument `archived`; for example, `list 1` is rejected.

Adds a student to TutorContacts. Only the student name is required; the remaining fields are optional.
Only `n/` is required. Every other prefix is optional. Prefixes may appear in any order, and `t/` may repeat.

| `n/` | Student name. Required; starts with a letter or digit; may contain letters (including accented letters), digits, spaces, hyphens (`-`), apostrophes (`'`), full stops (`.`), and slashes (`/`). `s/o`, `d/o`, `a/l`, and `a/p` in a name stay part of the name, for example `n/Raj s/o Kumar`. |
| `p/` | Student phone. Optional; digits only, 3 to 15 digits. |
| `e/` | Student email. Optional; a valid email address. |
| `s/` | Tutoring subject. Optional; nonblank text of at most 100 characters, without control characters. |
| `l/` | Education level. Optional; `P1`–`P6`, `S1`–`S5`, or `JC1`–`JC2`, regardless of input case. Displayed in uppercase. |
| `gn/` | Guardian name. Optional; uses the student-name rules. |
| `gp/` | Guardian phone. Optional; uses the student-phone rules and requires `gn/`. |
| `ge/` | Guardian email. Optional; uses the student-email rules and requires `gn/`. |
| `lf/` | Current learning focus. Optional; 1–200 characters without control characters. |
| `na/` | Next action. Optional; 1–200 characters without control characters. |
| `t/` | Optional tag; letters and digits only. Repeat `t/` to add more than one tag. |
Subject and education level may be supplied independently. Education levels are case-insensitive when entered and are
displayed in uppercase. If either field is omitted, the student card displays `Not provided` for that field.
Learning focus and next action may also be supplied independently. Ordinary spaces and punctuation are accepted.
Leading and trailing whitespace is removed, and repeated ordinary spaces are stored as one space. Control characters
within a value, including tabs and line breaks, are rejected, as are blank values and values longer than 200
characters. An omitted learning field is displayed as `Not provided`.
Leading and trailing whitespace around field values is ignored. Repeated whitespace inside names, guardian names,
and addresses is stored as one space. Repeated spaces inside subjects are stored as one space, but a tab, line break,
or other control character inside a subject is rejected. Whitespace within phone numbers, email addresses, education levels, and
tags is not accepted. Text before the first prefix and unknown prefix-like tokens such as `x/value` are rejected.
If a subject or address contains a separate one- or two-character token followed by `/`, enclose the complete value in
double quotes. For example, `add n/Alex s/"A l/Mathematics" a/"Block n/7"` stores the values without the quotes.
Words such as `Level/` are ordinary value text and do not need quotes. An unquoted unsupported token is still rejected.

`add n/ alex   tan` is rejected as a duplicate. Different students may share phone, email, and guardian details.
A guardian name may be supplied without guardian contact information.
